rows.speaker: خليل
rows.claim: Khalil reads al-khiṣām as a verbal noun meaning disputation, comparable to qitāl and ṭaʿām.
rows.anchor: قول خليل : إنه مصدر بمعنى المخاصمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One construction treats the genitive as if introduced by fī: he is most contentious in disputation.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه بمعنى { فى } والتقدير : ألد في الخصام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the dispute itself is called most contentious as an intensifying expression.
rows.anchor: أنه جعل الخصام ألد على سبيل المبالغة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes al-khiṣām as a plural of خصم, so the phrase means the most disputatious of opponents.
rows.anchor: أشد الخصوم خصومة ، وهذا قول الزجاج

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes say the verse was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, and also connect him with verses in al-Humaza and al-Qalam.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : هذه الآية نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid explains the phrase as a petitioner who does not act uprightly.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد { ألد الخصام } معناه : طالب لا يستقيم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the phrase as crooked in disputation.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي : أعوج الخصام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says he argues falsely, is harsh in disobeying God, eloquent in speech, yet ignorant in action.
rows.anchor: قتادة ألد الخصام معناه

rows.speaker: المنكرون للنظر والجدل
rows.claim: Opponents of rational inquiry cite the verse to argue that intense disputation is blameworthy, or reason would not be condemned.
rows.anchor: تمسك المنكرون للنظر والجدل بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers this objection by referring back to his discussion of the prohibition on disputation during pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: وجوابه ما تقدم في قوله : { ولا جدال في الحج }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrite speaks sweetly, invokes God as witness, and argues fiercely, while his heart conceals the opposite of his speech.
rows.anchor: كل ما ذكره باللسان فقلبه منطو على ضد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says al-Akhnas professed love for the Prophet and intent to believe, then after leaving burned Muslim crops and killed donkeys.
rows.anchor: فلما خرج من عنده مر بزرع للمسلمين فأحرق الزرع وقتل الحمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says that after Badr al-Akhnas attacked Banū Zuhra at night over a feud with Thaqīf, destroying livestock and crops.
rows.anchor: مر ببني زهرة وكان بينه وبين ثقيف خصومة فبيتهم ليلا وأهلك مواشيهم وأحرق زرعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second sense of corruption is spreading doubts among Muslims and devising ways to strengthen unbelief after leaving the Prophet.
rows.anchor: يشتغل بإدخال الشبه في قلوب المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious corruption divides people, severs kinship, and leads to bloodshed; 47:22 describes turning away from religion with those consequences.
rows.anchor: لأنه يوقع الاختلاف بين الناس ويفرق كلمتهم ويؤدي إلى أن يتبرأ بعضهم من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers corruption as spreading doubts because destroying crops and progeny is a distinct, subsequent evil rather than a restatement of corruption.
rows.anchor: حمل الفساد على هذا أولى من حمله على التخريب والنهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes تولى as becoming a ruler who acts like corrupt rulers, destroying crops and offspring.
rows.anchor: وإذا صار واليا فعل ما يفعله ولاة السوء من الفساد في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say an unjust ruler's oppression prevents rain by divine retribution, so crops and progeny perish.
rows.anchor: يظهر الظلم حتى يمنع الله بشؤم ظلمه القطر فيهلك الحرث والنسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading fits the passage better: he professes affection in the Prophet's presence, then seeks discord and corruption when absent.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أقرب إلى نظم الآية ، لأن المقصود بيان نفاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here saʿā means striving to provoke fighting; though it originally means walking quickly, it is metaphorical for stirring conflict and destruction among people.
rows.anchor: وأصل السعي هو المشي بسرعة ولكنه مستعار لإيقاع الفتنة

rows.speaker: من فسر الفساد بالتخريب
rows.claim: On the physical-destruction reading, the verse first states corruption generally, then specifies it as destroying crops and offspring.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكره ثانيا على سبيل التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the doubt-spreading reading, false religion begins with doubts and proceeds to evil deeds; Rāzī calls this interpretation preferable.
rows.anchor: ولا شك في أن هذا التفسير أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the report that al-Akhnas burned Muslim crops and killed donkeys, al-ḥarth means cultivated crops and al-nasl means the donkeys.
rows.anchor: المراد بالحرث الزرع ، وبالنسل تلك الحمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥarth is what is cultivated, extending to everything plowed and planted among the kinds of vegetation; it can also mean plowing itself.
rows.anchor: وهو يقع على كل ما يحرث ويرزع من أصناف النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nasl means offspring and derives from emergence or falling out, like shed feathers, camel fur, or donkey hair; people are Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: والنسل في اللغة : الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root idea of nasl is خروج, and offspring are called nasl because the child emerges from the father's back and mother's womb.
rows.anchor: النسل الولد لخروجه من ظهر الأب وبطن الأم وسقوطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the reported night attack on a Thaqīf group, exegetes offer different referents for al-ḥarth.
rows.anchor: أن الأخنس بيت على قوم ثقيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that account, al-ḥarth may mean women, by analogy with wives being a field for their husbands.
rows.anchor: المراد بالحرث : إما النسوان لقوله تعالى : { نساؤكم حرث لكم }

rows.speaker: قوم من المفسرين
rows.claim: Alternatively, some exegetes take al-ḥarth as men, because men plow the land of reproduction.
rows.anchor: أو الرجال وهو قول قوم من المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the account of the attack on Thaqīf, al-nasl refers to the children.
rows.anchor: وأما النسل فالمراد منه الصبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whichever interpretation is chosen, the phrase describes the greatest possible corruption: destroying plants and animals, or destroying animal life at its roots and branches.
rows.anchor: إهلاك النبات والحيوان ، وعلى التفسير الثاني : إهلاك الحيوان بأصله وفرعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compact phrase is especially eloquent, using few words to convey extreme destruction and emphasis.
rows.anchor: من الألفاظ الفصيحة جدا الدالة مع اختصارها على المبالغة الكثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī compares this concise expression with other brief Qur'anic descriptions of Paradise's pleasures and the earth's water and pasture.
rows.anchor: ونظيره في الاختصار ما قاله في صفة الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If destruction is coordinated with saʿā, the verse states the aim of his striving, not that destruction occurred; as an independent clause it states actual destruction, but the first syntax is preferable.
rows.anchor: والأول أولى ، وإن كانت الأخبار المذكورة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read the verb actively with the crops and offspring as its subject, meaning that they perish.
rows.anchor: قرأ بعضهم { ويهلك الحرث والنسل }

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ya-hlak with fatḥa on the lām, a dialectal pattern like abā ya'bā.
rows.anchor: الحسن بفتح اللام من يهلك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A passive reading of يهلك is also transmitted from al-Ḥasan.
rows.anchor: وروي عنه { ويهلك } على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that love means will: 24:19 uses love for wishing indecency to spread, and hatred is presented as love's opposite.
rows.anchor: استدلت المعتزلة على أن الله تعالى لا يريد القبائح بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الرسول عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says God loved worship without associating anything with Him and sincere counsel to rulers, and disliked gossip, wasting wealth, and excessive questions; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: نقل عن الرسول عليه السلام أنه قال : ( إن الله أحب لكم ثلاثا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: If love is will, the verse means God does not will corruption, like 40:31; the Muʿtazilites infer that the described corruption occurred without His will and was not created by Him.
rows.anchor: فدل على أن ذلك الواقع وقع لا بإرادة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الأصحاب
rows.claim: Rāzī's Ashʿarite colleagues answer in two ways: love means praise and exaltation rather than will, or, even if love means will, the definite article does not make the statement universal.
rows.anchor: والأصحاب أجابوا عنه بوجهين الأول : أن المحبة غير الإرادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human capacity and motives are apt for good and evil; if evil is preferred without a cause there is no Creator, while a determining cause must come from God or entail an infinite regress, so God determines the preference for evil.
rows.anchor: إن وقع لا لعلة لزم نفي الصانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God knows corruption will occur, willing it not to occur would amount to willing His own knowledge to become ignorance, which is impossible.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنه عالم بوقوع الفساد

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the Messenger called the man to abandon these acts, but pride and disdain led him to wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : قوله تعالى : { وإذا قيل له اتق الله أخذته العزة } معناه أن رسول الله دعاه إلى ترك هذه الأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī calls al-Wāḥidī's explanation weak: the verse does not say who told him to fear God or even establish that this occurred; a report would be needed, though the Prophet called everyone to piety.
rows.anchor: هذا التفسير ضعيف ، لأن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God applies to all five faults: worldly ambition, false oaths, obstinate defense of falsehood, corruption, and destruction of crops and progeny.
rows.anchor: وجب أن يحمل على الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One idiomatic reading compares the phrase to compelling someone to do something: arrogance impels him to sin, namely ignoring and refusing to hear the admonisher.
rows.anchor: أن هذا مأخوذ من قولهم أخذت فلانا بأن يعمل كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, arrogance has become attached to him or overtaken him, as fever does; his sinful pride arises from disbelief, ignorance, and failure to consider proofs.
rows.anchor: أي لزمته يقال : أخذته الحمى أي لزمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ can mean because of or function like lām, as in saying that one acted because of someone or punished him for his offense.
rows.anchor: والباء ههنا في معنى اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pride caused by unbelief is like the state described in 38:2, where disbelievers are in arrogance and opposition.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى : { بل الذين كفروا فى عزة وشقاق }

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes gloss the phrase as Hell sufficing him as recompense and punishment, as a dirham can suffice someone or God can suffice us.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : كافيه جهنم جزاء له وعذابا

rows.speaker: يونس وأكثر النحويين
rows.claim: Yūnus and most grammarians say Jahannam is a foreign name for the fire of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: جهنم فقال يونس وأكثر النحويين : هي اسم للنار

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others regard Jahannam as an Arabic name for Hell, derived from the great depth of its pit.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون . جهنم اسم عربي سميت نار الآخرة بها

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: Ruʾba's phrase about a deep well supplies evidence for the Arabic root sense of great depth.
rows.anchor: حكى عن رؤبة أنه قال : ركية جهنام بريد بعيدة القعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes al-mihād and tamhīd as laying or preparing, from a bed; 51:48 calls the earth spread out and its spreaders good, and 30:44 speaks of preparing for oneself.
rows.anchor: أن المهاد والتمهيد : التوطئة ، وأصله من المهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading makes al-mihād an evil resting place, as in the verse calling Hell an evil settlement.
rows.anchor: أي لبئس المستقر كقوله : { جهنم يصلونها وبئس القرار }

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars understand al-mihād as a sleeping bed: the person punished in Hell is laid upon its fire as his bed.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء : المهاد الفراش للنوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects the anomalous reading: any Qur'anic reading must be established by tawātur, and this one is not transmitted that way.
rows.anchor: القراءة الشاذة مردودة لأن كل ما كان قرآنا وجب أن يثبت بالتواتر فحيث لم يثبت بالتواتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says Abū Ḥanīfa especially should reject this reading, since he relied on the same letter to argue that the basmala is not Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وأولى الناس بهذا أبو حنيفة ، فإنه بهذا الحرف تمسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's three contextual indications show that the return (fayʾa) does not occur within the waiting period, so a contrary anomalous reading is invalid.
rows.anchor: فالقراءة الشاذة لما كانت مخالفة لها وجب القطع بفسادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A woman divorced before marriage is divorced only in the lexical sense, not by legal convention, and no waiting period is required by consensus.
rows.anchor: فهي مطلقة بحسب اللغة ، لكنها غير مطلقة بحسب عرف الشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A married woman divorced before consummation has no waiting period, as stated in 33:49.
rows.anchor: فإن لم تكن مدخولا بها لم تجب العدة عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A consummated divorcee who is pregnant waits until delivery, not through menstrual cycles, according to 65:4.
rows.anchor: فإن كانت حاملا فعدتها بوضع الحمل لا بالإقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nonpregnant woman who cannot menstruate because of extreme youth or age counts her waiting period in months, not quruʾ.
rows.anchor: فإن امتنع الحيض في حقها إما للصغر المفرط ، أو للكبر المفرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An enslaved woman counts two quruʾ, not three.
rows.anchor: فإن كانت رقيقة كانت عدتها بقرأين لا بثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three-quruʾ rule applies when a woman is married, divorced after consummation, not pregnant, menstruating, and free.
rows.anchor: فعند اجتماع هذه الصفات كانت عدتها بالإقراء الثلاثة على ما بين الله حكمها في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says a general term should retain a majority of its cases after specification, like calling a mostly black garment black; this verse appears to exclude five groups and leave one.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية ليست كذلك فإنكم أخرجتم من عمومها خمسة أقسام وتركتم قسما واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A woman divorced before marriage is outside the legal wording because such a woman is not called a divorced woman in this usage.
rows.anchor: أما الأجنبية فخارجة عن اللفظ فإن الأجنبية لا يقال فيها : إنها مطلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context excludes an unconsummated marriage: the waiting period clears the womb, and that need arises only after prior intercourse.
rows.anchor: وأما غير المدخول بها فالقرينة تخرجها لأن المقصود من العدة براءة الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pregnant and menopausal women are outside the quruʾ rule because menstrual cycles do not occur for them.
rows.anchor: وأما الحامل والآيسة فهما خارجتان عن اللفظ لأن إيجاب الاعتداد بالإقراء إنما يكون حيث تحصل الإقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enslaved women are rare in marriage, so most cases remain within the verse's general wording.
rows.anchor: وأما الرقيقة فتزويجها كالنادر فثبت أن الأعم الأغلب باق تحت هذا العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although يتربصن is grammatically a report, it means a command; the declarative form avoids implying that the waiting period counts only when begun intentionally.
rows.anchor: قوله : { يتربصن } لا شك أنه خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a husband dies and his wife does not learn of it until the waiting period expires, the period still counts whether she knew, intended, consented, or was unwilling.
rows.anchor: وعرف أنه مهما انقضت هذه العدة حصل المقصود

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf says the declarative form intensifies the command and signals urgency, as though the women had already obeyed; a prayer for mercy uses the same form in confidence of response.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : التعبير عن الأمر بصيغة الخبر يفيد تأكيد الأمر

rows.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
rows.claim: In Dalāʾil al-Iʿjāz, ʿAbd al-Qāhir says putting the subject first strengthens the statement; this can single out the actor or establish the actor's characteristic action.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ عبد القاهر الجرجاني في كتاب ( دلائل الإعجاز ) : إنك إذا قدمت الاسم

rows.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
rows.claim: The fronted subject can specify that actor as uniquely performing the action, or simply establish that the action is the subject's characteristic habit.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون لتخصيص ذلك الفاعل بذلك الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī illustrates subject-first exclusivity with 'I write to the ruler on this important matter,' while a statement that someone gives generously confirms a habit without claiming exclusivity.
rows.anchor: كقولك : أنا أكتب في المهم الفلاني إلى السلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī cites 16:20 and 5:61 as further examples of clauses with the subject put first to affirm what is said about it.
rows.anchor: ومثله قوله تعالى : { والذين يدعون من دون الله لا يخلقون شيئا وهم }

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The anonymous poet's line front-loads the subject in a statement praising the two men, serving as an example of the construction under discussion.
rows.anchor: هما يلبسان المجد أحسن لبسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming the subject first creates anticipation for the predicate; when it arrives, it is received more forcefully, confirming the statement and removing doubt.
rows.anchor: فيحصل في العقل شوق إلى معرفة ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning their selves incites women to wait by urging them to restrain their longing for men and overcome their own desires.
rows.anchor: في ذكر الأنفس تهييج لهن على التربص وزيادة بعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī contrasts the wording here with 2:226, which commands a four-month waiting period without mentioning the selves.
rows.anchor: كما قيل : { تربص أربعة أشهر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although anfus is a plural of paucity and quruʾ a plural of abundance, Arabic freely exchanges the two plural patterns, or quruʾ may simply be the more usual plural of qarʾ.
rows.anchor: يتسعون في ذلك فيستعملون كل واحد من الجمعين مكان الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The number uses the masculine form thalāthata because quruʾ is grammatically masculine.
rows.anchor: لأنه أتبع تذكير اللفظ ولفظ القروء مذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no dispute that qarʾ can name both menstruation and the period of purity between menstruations.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف أن اسم القرء يقع على الحيض والطهر

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda calls al-aqrāʾ a word of opposite meanings; the better-known analysis treats it as genuinely applying to both, like shafaq for redness and whiteness.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : الإقراء من الأضداد في كلام / العرب

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Some make menstruation the literal meaning and purity figurative; others reverse the relation.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون إنه حقيقة في الحيض ، مجاز في الطهر

rows.speaker: قائلون
rows.claim: Another group says the word has one underlying shared sense applicable to both menstruation and purity.
rows.anchor: وقال قائلون : إنه موضوع بحيثية معنى واحد مشترك

rows.speaker: الأصمعي والأخفش والفراء والكسائي
rows.claim: The first shared-sense explanation is gathering: blood gathers in the womb during menstruation and in the body during purity.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الأصمعي والأخفش والفراء والكسائي
